correctness.rationale: The Gram inverse is solved on two adjacent rows by a strictly diagonally dominant bi-infinite tridiagonal Jacobi recurrence; all three critical junction equations and one extra neighbor equation were verified symbolically. An exact signed linear-interpolant absolute-integral formula, geometric tail sums, and quadratic-field algebra give two factorizations. Every denominator is positive for τ>0, and numerator signs give the two disjoint intervals. The τ=1 case is exactly 2 by translation invariance and convexity. Nine exact symbolic checks, twelve sign comparisons and six finite-section comparisons were run successfully. Finite tests alone would not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The spline projection norm 2 is a canonical uniform-mesh sharp threshold, with practical stability significance. Proving strict loss of this threshold for any one-cell distortion, arbitrarily close to unit length, is a natural complete one-defect classification. The additional short-cell versus long-cell witness-location reversal is a non-obvious structural distinction, supported by exact formulas. The global norm for τ≠1 remains unknown and is not needed for this value claim.
